subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Coffee-to-Water Ratio
description: A fast breakdown of The Coffee-to-Water Ratio for builders.

hook.text: Use too much water and coffee is watery. Too little and it's overwhelmingly strong. Ratio is everything.

buildup.text: The Specialty Coffee Association standard is 1:15 to 1:18—one gram of coffee per 15–18 grams of water.

discovery.text: Espresso is much more concentrated at 1:2—18 grams of coffee yielding 36 grams of liquid.

twist.text: Changing the ratio changes extraction too. More water means more extraction, not just more volume.

climax.text: A kitchen scale costing $15 improves coffee more than $100 worth of fancy beans. Precision beats expense.

punchline.text: Weigh your coffee. Weigh your water. Taste the difference.

quiz.question: What is the SCA standard coffee-to-water ratio for drip?

details.summary: The standard specialty coffee ratio is about 1 gram of coffee to 15-18 grams of water. This ratio, combined with extraction percentage, determines the strength and flavor balance of the cup. Using a scale to measure dose and water volume is the simplest path to consistent results.
details.whyItMatters: Ratio is the foundation of repeatable brewing. Once you find your preferred ratio, you can replicate your favorite cup every time.
takeaways: The standard ratio is roughly 1:15 to 1:18 coffee to water
Stronger coffee uses more grounds, not longer brew time
A kitchen scale is the most useful brewing tool

faq.question: What ratio should beginners start with?
faq.answer: Start with 1:16, meaning 1 gram of coffee per 16 grams of water. For a typical mug, that is about 15 grams of coffee to 240 grams of water. Adjust stronger or weaker based on taste preference.

faq.question: Does the ratio change for different brew methods?
faq.answer: Slightly. Espresso uses a concentrated ratio around 1:2. Pour-over and drip use 1:15 to 1:17. French press tends toward 1:15 for fuller body. Cold brew uses 1:8 because it is diluted before drinking. The principles are the same; the numbers shift.
